Corrected age = chronological age minus 40 weeks
Conceptional age = gestational age + chronological age
questions.explanation: Record gestational, chronological and postmenstrual age in weeks. Postmenstrual age is gestational age plus chronological age; the AAP advises against the term conceptional age.
questions.memoryAid: POST-MENSTRUAL = GA + CA. 'Conceptional' is OUT.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: What sensitivity does Guideline 6 require when recording for electrocerebral inactivity?
options: 2 µV peak to peak for 10 min
questions.explanation: Record at 2 µV/mm or more sensitive (for example 1 µV/mm) for at least 30 min, with a calibration of 2 or 5 µV. Note the unit: 2 µV/mm is the sensitivity; 2 µV peak to peak is the voltage threshold for ECI.
questions.memoryAid: ECI = TWO and THIRTY: 2 µV/mm for 30 minutes.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: What interelectrode distance does Guideline 6 require for ECI montages?
options: At most 5 cm, using closely spaced pairs
At least 10 cm, using double-distance pairs such as Fp1-C3
Any distance, as long as all channels are referential
questions.explanation: Longer distances record more of a low-voltage field, so ECI montages use pairs at least 10 cm apart (double-distance links such as Fp1-C3 and C3-O1). A full electrode set including Fz, Cz and Pz is needed; a 1- or 2-channel device is not acceptable.
questions.memoryAid: TEN cm APART to hear a whisper.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: How is the integrity of the whole recording system tested during an ECI study?
options: Touching each electrode to make an artifact
Raising the high-frequency filter to 100 Hz
Checking every impedance once at the start
questions.explanation: Touching each electrode in turn proves that every channel is connected and displaying. Impedances must be between 100 and 10,000 Ω; machine noise is checked with a 10,000 Ω resistor across the inputs, and an ECG and noncephalic (dorsum of the hand) monitor are added.
questions.memoryAid: TOUCH TEST: tap each lead, see it jump, then you know it is live.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Which filter settings does Guideline 6 allow during an ECI recording?
options: LFF 5 Hz to remove sweat; HFF 70 Hz
HFF no lower than 30 Hz; LFF no higher than 1 Hz
Notch on throughout; HFF and LFF unchanged
HFF 15 Hz to remove muscle; LFF 1 Hz
questions.explanation: HFF no lower than 30 Hz and LFF no higher than 1 Hz. If the notch filter is used, part of the record must also be made without it. Intense somatosensory, auditory and visual stimuli are applied and annotated.
questions.memoryAid: ECI filters: THIRTY up, ONE down, and show it once WITHOUT the notch.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: If ECI is in doubt, when should the study be repeated?
options: 6 h later in adults, 24 h in children
24 h later in adults, 6 h in children
Never; a single study is always final
questions.explanation: Guideline 6: repeat after at least 6 h in adults and at least 24 h in neonates and children. Also document temperature, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, all medications, the last sedative dose and toxicology, because drugs and hypothermia can mimic ECI.
questions.memoryAid: SIX hours for grown-ups, a whole DAY for the young.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: In which section of a Guideline 7 report does premedication and its dose belong?
questions.explanation: The five sections are History, Technical Description, EEG Description, Impression and Clinical Correlation. The technical description covers date and place, number of electrodes, 10-20 or 10-10 placement, extra or moved electrodes, premedication with dose, sleep deprivation and state.
questions.memoryAid: Five parts, H-T-E-I-C: 'Have The EEG Interpreted Clearly'.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: How does Guideline 7 structure the Impression?
options: A full description of the background, then the artifacts
Normal or abnormal first, then the main abnormalities ranked
The technologist's opinion, then the physician's
questions.explanation: The impression states normal or abnormal first, then ranks the main abnormalities (preferably no more than three or four). The clinical correlation explains the meaning in plain language and gives no specific treatment orders.
questions.memoryAid: IMPRESSION: verdict FIRST, then the TOP three.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: According to Guideline 7, when should artifacts be mentioned in the report?
options: Only when caused by equipment failure
When they mimic, swamp, block or help the reading
Every artifact, each listed with its time
Not at all, since artifacts are not cerebral
questions.explanation: Artifacts are reported when they mimic cerebral activity, are excessive, interfere (more than 50% of the tracing in more than 50% of electrodes) or are diagnostically useful.
questions.memoryAid: Report the artifact that FOOLS, FLOODS, BLOCKS or HELPS.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: The 2021 ACNS Critical Care EEG Terminology applies to which patients?
questions.explanation: The 2021 terminology (Hirsch et al.) replaced the 2012 version and is used for all ages except neonates, who have a separate ACNS terminology. It added ESz, ESE, ECSz, ECSE, BIRDs, IIC, UI, identical bursts, CAPE and extreme delta brush.
questions.memoryAid: 2021 is for EVERYONE but the NEWBORN.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Rhythmic delta is bilaterally synchronous and symmetric but limited to both frontal regions. What is Main Term 1?
questions.explanation: Generalized means any bilaterally synchronous and symmetric pattern, even with a restricted field such as bifrontal. A region at least 50% higher in voltage earns a predominance label: frontally, occipitally or midline predominant.
questions.memoryAid: SYNC + SYMMETRIC = G, even if it only covers the FRONT.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: A bilateral pattern is synchronous but clearly and consistently higher on the right. How is it classed?
questions.explanation: Generalized must also be symmetric. A bilateral pattern clearly and consistently larger on one side (bilateral asymmetric), or with a consistent lead-in from the same side (bilateral asynchronous), is lateralized. Shifting predominance that is not consistently (over 80%) on one side stays generalized.
questions.memoryAid: LOPSIDED is LATERALIZED, even when both sides fire.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Two independent periodic patterns occur at the same time in the same hemisphere. Which Main Term 1 is used?
questions.explanation: UI, new in 2021, is two independent patterns in the same hemisphere at the same time. BI is one in each hemisphere at the same time. Mf needs at least three independent lateralized patterns with at least one in each hemisphere.
questions.memoryAid: U = Unilateral = ONE side, TWO patterns. B = Both sides. Mf = Many (3+).
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: How many independent lateralized patterns are needed for 'multifocal'?
options: Three or more, with each hemisphere involved
Two or more, both in the same hemisphere
Two, with one in each hemisphere
questions.explanation: Multifocal is at least three independent lateralized patterns, at least one in each hemisphere, all occurring at the same time. Independent patterns at different times (left one hour, right later) are two lateralized patterns, not BI or Mf.
questions.memoryAid: MULTI = THREE or more, and BOTH sides represented.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Sharp waves each followed by a slow wave repeat with a clear, flat interval between complexes. Which Main Term 2 fits?
questions.explanation: SW requires the slow wave to be followed immediately by the next complex, with no interval. Once there is a clear interval between discharges recurring at nearly regular intervals, the pattern is PDs.
questions.memoryAid: A GAP makes it PERIODIC. No gap = SW.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: What is the minimum duration for a pattern to qualify as rhythmic or periodic?
questions.explanation: At least 6 consecutive cycles (for example 1 Hz for 6 s, or 3 Hz for 2 s). Three cycles is the minimum for each step of evolution, a common source of confusion.
questions.memoryAid: SIX to COUNT, THREE to STEP.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: How does the 2021 terminology define 'nearly regular' (rhythmic or periodic)?
options: Each discharge has the same number of phases
Period varies under 10% across the pattern
Every cycle is exactly the same length
Period varies under 50% in most cycle pairs
questions.explanation: Rhythmic or periodic means the period varies by less than 50% from one cycle to the next in most (over 50%) cycle pairs. It does not require identical cycles, a fixed number of phases or a fixed duration.
questions.memoryAid: Under HALF a change, in more than HALF the pairs.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Rhythmic, regular 1.5 Hz delta is seen over the left hemisphere only. What is it named?
questions.explanation: Lateralized (L) + rhythmic delta activity (RDA) = LRDA. RDA must have a fairly uniform shape and duration with no interval between waves, at 0.5 to 4 Hz; irregular or polymorphic delta is not RDA.
questions.memoryAid: Build the NAME like LEGO: where (L) + what (RDA).
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: A pattern is present in 30% of a recording epoch. What is its prevalence?
questions.explanation: Prevalence: continuous at least 90%; abundant 50 to 89%; frequent 10 to 49%; occasional 1 to 9%; rare under 1%.
questions.memoryAid: Prevalence 1-10-50-90: rare, occasional, FREQUENT, abundant, continuous.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: A run of a pattern lasts 5 minutes. Which duration category applies?
questions.explanation: Duration: very long at least 1 h; long 10 to 59 min; intermediate 1 to 9.9 min; brief 10 to 59 s; very brief under 10 s.
questions.memoryAid: Seconds BRIEF, minutes MIDDLE, tens of minutes LONG, an hour VERY long.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: A periodic discharge has a duration of 120 ms measured at the baseline. How is its sharpness classed?
questions.explanation: Sharpness applies to PDs and SW only and is measured at the baseline: spiky under 70 ms, sharp 70 to 200 ms, sharply contoured (sharp shape but too long), blunt (smooth or sinusoidal).
questions.memoryAid: Same cut-offs as spikes and sharp waves: 70 and 200 ms.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: A pattern's discharges measure 90 µV peak to trough on longitudinal bipolar. Which absolute amplitude category applies?
questions.explanation: Absolute amplitude: very low under 20 µV, low 20 to 49 µV, medium 50 to 149 µV, high at least 150 µV, measured peak to trough in longitudinal bipolar. Relative amplitude (PDs only) compares the discharge with the background between discharges: 2 or less, or more than 2.
questions.memoryAid: 20-50-150: very low, low, MEDIUM, high.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Which change counts as evolution under the 2021 terminology?
options: A steady rise in amplitude over 2 minutes
A single 1 Hz change in frequency
Two 0.5 Hz steps one way, 3+ cycles each
Three back-and-forth changes in a minute
questions.explanation: Evolution needs at least two unequivocal sequential changes in one category (frequency, morphology or location), each step lasting at least 3 cycles, without the feature staying unchanged for 5 min or more. Amplitude change alone is not evolution. Back-and-forth changes are fluctuation.
questions.memoryAid: EVOLVING goes ONE WAY, TWO steps, 3 cycles each. Bigger is not evolving.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: A pattern changes 1 to 1.5 to 1 to 1.5 Hz, each change within a minute of the last. How is it described?
questions.explanation: Fluctuating means three or more changes no more than 1 min apart in frequency (at least 0.5 Hz), morphology or location (at least one interelectrode distance), without meeting the criteria for evolution. Static is neither evolving nor fluctuating.
questions.memoryAid: FLUCTUATING goes UP and DOWN like a yo-yo; EVOLVING marches ONE way.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: LPDs appear reproducibly each time the nurse rouses the patient. How is this coded?
questions.explanation: Stimulus-induced (SI-) means reproducibly brought on or made worse by an alerting stimulus; stimulus-terminated (ST-) means reproducibly stopped. SIRPIDs is the umbrella term, but the specific pattern should be named, with the type of stimulus recorded.
questions.memoryAid: SI = Stimulus IN (starts it); ST = Stimulus sTops it.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Which plus modifier can be applied to rhythmic delta activity but not to periodic discharges?
questions.explanation: +F (superimposed fast) applies to PDs or RDA; +R applies to PDs only; +S applies to RDA only; combined forms are +FR for PDs and +FS for RDA. Plus modifiers never apply to SW. A pattern that is both PDs and RDA with similar prominence is coded PDs+R, not RDA+S.
questions.memoryAid: PDs get R, RDA gets S; F fits both; SW gets NOTHING.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Abundant rhythmic delta with fast activity locked to each delta wave is called what?
options: Delta brush of prematurity, a normal variant
Extreme delta brush, a subtype of +F
questions.explanation: Extreme delta brush is a subtype of +F: abundant or continuous RDA+F (or blunt-delta PDs+F) with fast activity locked to the delta wave, classically described in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
questions.memoryAid: EXTREME delta BRUSH = a fast BRISTLE riding EVERY delta wave.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: What is the current 2021 name for the pattern once called FIRDA?
questions.explanation: FIRDA became frontally predominant GRDA. Other replacements: PLEDs became LPDs, BIPLEDs became BIPDs, GPEDs became GPDs, semirhythmic delta became quasi-RDA, and 'subclinical' seizure became 'nonconvulsive'. The 'E' for epileptiform was dropped because many periodic patterns are not epileptic.
questions.memoryAid: Old letters OUT: PLEDs → LPDs, FIRDA → frontal GRDA, drop the E.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: How does the 2021 terminology handle 'triphasic waves'?
questions.explanation: Triphasic morphology is a minor modifier, not a pattern name: negative-positive-negative, each phase longer than the one before, with the positive phase highest.
questions.memoryAid: TRIPHASIC is a SHAPE, not a NAME: GPDs with triphasic morphology.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Which pattern meets the 2021 definition of an electrographic seizure (ESz)?
options: Rhythmic delta lasting at least 5 s
Discharges over 2.5 Hz for 10 s or more
questions.explanation: ESz: epileptiform discharges averaging more than 2.5 Hz for at least 10 s (more than 25 discharges in 10 s), or any pattern with definite evolution lasting at least 10 s. PDs or SW above 2.5 Hz for 10 s or more are seizures, not PDs.
questions.memoryAid: Seizure 10 / 2.5 / 25: over 2.5 Hz, 10 seconds, 25 discharges.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: When does seizure activity become electrographic status epilepticus (ESE)?
options: 10 continuous min, or 20% of any hour
questions.explanation: ESE is ESz for at least 10 continuous minutes, or for a total of at least 20% of any 60-minute period. A frequent mistake is to give 30 minutes.
questions.memoryAid: TEN straight, or a FIFTH of an hour (12 minutes total).
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Which statement about an electroclinical seizure (ECSz) is correct?
options: Only when EEG improves and the patient does not
Any length, if a clinical sign is time-locked
Only when the rhythm is faster than 4 Hz
At least 10 s, the same as an ESz
questions.explanation: ECSz is any EEG pattern with a definite time-locked clinical correlate (any duration), or EEG and clinical improvement after a parenteral antiseizure medication. An ECSz can be shorter than 10 s; an ESz cannot. 'Nonconvulsive' is preferred over 'subclinical'.
questions.memoryAid: Clinical sign + EEG = seizure at ANY length. EEG alone needs 10 s.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: With bilateral tonic-clonic activity, how long must an electroclinical seizure last to be electroclinical status epilepticus?
questions.explanation: ECSE is ECSz for at least 10 continuous minutes or at least 20% of any 60 minutes, but with bilateral tonic-clonic activity 5 continuous minutes is enough, matching the ILAE 2015 t1 of 5 min for tonic-clonic status (t2 30 min).
questions.memoryAid: CONVULSING? FIVE minutes is status.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Which description fits BIRDs (brief potentially ictal rhythmic discharges)?
options: Over 4 Hz, 0.5 to under 10 s, with evolution, a match or sharp contour
Periodic discharges at 1 Hz lasting more than 10 seconds
Any normal variant that lasts less than 10 seconds
Rhythmic delta under 4 Hz lasting about one minute
questions.explanation: BIRDs: focal or generalized rhythmic activity over 4 Hz (at least 6 waves at a regular rate), lasting 0.5 s to under 10 s, not a normal variant or part of burst suppression, without a definite clinical correlate, and with evolution, a match to the patient's discharges or seizures, or sharp contour. The same evolving rhythm for 10 s or more is a seizure.
questions.memoryAid: BIRDs are FAST and BRIEF: over 4 Hz, under 10 s.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: BIRDs that are sharply contoured but neither evolve nor match the patient's seizures are classed as what?
questions.explanation: Definite BIRDs show evolution, or the same morphology and location as the patient's interictal discharges or seizures. Sharply contoured BIRDs without either are possible BIRDs.
questions.memoryAid: EVOLVES or MATCHES = DEFINITE; only SHARP = POSSIBLE.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Which pattern meets criterion A of the ictal-interictal continuum (IIC)?
options: Periodic discharges averaging more than 1.0 and up to 2.5 Hz over 10 seconds
GRDA at 1.5 Hz with no plus modifier
Periodic discharges averaging more than 2.5 Hz for 10 seconds
questions.explanation: IIC criterion A: any PD or SW pattern averaging more than 1.0 and up to 2.5 Hz over 10 s (more than 10 and up to 25 discharges in 10 s). Criterion B is 0.5 to 1 Hz with a plus modifier or fluctuation. Above 2.5 Hz for 10 s it is already a seizure, and IIC excludes anything meeting ESz or ESE.
questions.memoryAid: IIC sits BETWEEN 1 and 2.5 Hz: below a seizure, above plain PDs.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Under IIC criterion C, which rhythmic delta pattern is excluded?
questions.explanation: Criterion C covers lateralized RDA (LRDA, BIRDA, UIRDA, MfRDA) averaging more than 1 Hz for at least 10 s with a plus modifier or fluctuation. GRDA is not included. IIC is a purely electrographic term (possible ESz or ESE), not a diagnosis.
questions.memoryAid: IIC rhythmic delta must be ONE-SIDED: GRDA does not count.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: The left hemisphere is consistently 60% lower in voltage than the right on a referential montage. How is the symmetry classed?
options: It cannot be classed without a bipolar montage
questions.explanation: Marked asymmetry is a voltage difference of 50% or more, or a frequency difference of more than 1 Hz. Mild is under 50% or 0.5 to 1 Hz. Voltage asymmetry is judged on an appropriate referential recording, because bipolar subtraction can hide or create asymmetry.
questions.memoryAid: HALF or more = MARKED; check it REFERENTIALLY.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Which rule applies to the posterior dominant rhythm in the 2021 terminology?
options: It counts whether or not it blocks with eye opening
It is measured in the first half-second after eye closure
It must block with eye opening; measured over 1 s after closure
It is reported to the nearest 2 Hz, without reactivity
questions.explanation: The PDR must attenuate with eye opening to qualify. Measure it more than 1 s after eye closure to avoid alpha squeak, and report it to the nearest 0.5 Hz as present, absent or unclear.
questions.memoryAid: WAIT ONE SECOND after closing: squeak first, true rhythm after.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Bursts of 2 s alternate with 8 s of suppression. How is continuity classed?
questions.explanation: Continuity by percentage of the record attenuated or suppressed: continuous under 1%, nearly continuous 1 to 9%, discontinuous 10 to 49%, burst attenuation or suppression 50 to 99%, attenuation or suppression over 99%. Here 8 of every 10 s (80%) is suppressed.
questions.memoryAid: Continuity 1-10-50-99.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: What is the difference between 'suppression' and 'attenuation' in the 2021 terminology?
options: Suppression < 20 µV; attenuation < 50 µV whatever the background
They are synonyms used for the same low-voltage periods
Suppression lasts longer; voltage does not separate the two
Suppression < 10 µV; attenuation ≥ 10 µV but < 50% of background
questions.explanation: Suppression: lower-voltage periods under 10 µV. Attenuation: lower-voltage periods of at least 10 µV but under 50% of the higher-voltage background. For overall voltage, suppressed means all activity under 10 µV and low means most activity under 20 µV.
questions.memoryAid: UNDER 10 = SUPPRESSED. Above 10 but under half = ATTENUATED.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: What makes a waveform a 'burst' rather than a 'discharge'?
options: It lasts at least 2 s regardless of phases
It lasts at least 0.5 s and has at least 4 phases
questions.explanation: A burst averages at least 0.5 s and has at least 4 phases (at least 3 baseline crossings); shorter or with fewer phases it is a discharge. Bursts can last up to 30 s, and burst and interburst durations are reported.
questions.memoryAid: BURST = half a second and FOUR phases.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: When are bursts called 'identical' in the 2021 terminology?
options: First 0.5 s matches in all channels in over 90% of bursts
At least two bursts in the record contain spikes
Every burst has the same peak amplitude throughout
questions.explanation: Identical bursts (new in 2021): the first 0.5 s or more of each burst, or of each stereotyped cluster, looks similar in all channels in over 90% of bursts. Highly epileptiform bursts have 2 or more spikes or sharp waves in most bursts at 1 Hz or faster, or a rhythmic ictal-appearing pattern.
questions.memoryAid: IDENTICAL = the same OPENING half-second, 9 times in 10.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: During reactivity testing, only eye-blink and muscle artifact appear after a sternal rub. How is this recorded?
options: SIRPIDs-only, because a stimulus was given
Reactive if the artifact lasts over 1 s
Unreactive: artifact alone does not count
questions.explanation: Reactivity is a change in cerebral EEG activity (voltage or frequency, including attenuation) after stimulation. Muscle or eye-blink artifact alone does not count. Use escalating visual, auditory, tactile and noxious stimuli, annotate each, repeat a second round of noxious stimuli if unreactive, and record sedatives and paralytics.
questions.memoryAid: REACTIVITY lives in the BRAIN waves, not in the BLINKS.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Two background patterns, each at least 10 s long, alternate regularly for at least 6 cycles. What is this called?
questions.explanation: CAPE: two background patterns, each at least 10 s, alternating regularly for at least 6 cycles. State changes (which replaced 'variability') need at least 2 sustained background types related to alertness or stimulation, each lasting at least 60 s.
questions.memoryAid: CAPE = a 10-second SWING, six times over.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: Sporadic epileptiform discharges occur about twice a minute. What is their prevalence category?
options: Frequent (at least 1 per minute but under 1 per 10 s)
Occasional (at least 1 per hour but under 1 per minute)
questions.explanation: Sporadic discharges: abundant at least 1 per 10 s (not periodic); frequent at least 1 per minute but under 1 per 10 s; occasional at least 1 per hour but under 1 per minute; rare under 1 per hour.
questions.memoryAid: Per 10 s ABUNDANT, per minute FREQUENT, per hour OCCASIONAL.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: How often should the technologist check recording quality during continuous ICU EEG (2015 consensus)?
questions.explanation: Stay at the bedside for the first 20 min and test reactivity, then check recording quality at least twice daily, impedance and scalp daily, and re-gel as needed. Physicians review the first 30 to 60 min as soon as possible, then at least twice daily, with a written report at least every 24 h.
questions.memoryAid: cEEG: 20 minutes at the bed, TWICE a day the check, a report EVERY day.
questions.author: NeuroLinea Focus Drills (AI-drafted, fact-checked; requires expert review)

questions.stem: A patient for cEEG has a right craniotomy. How should the electrodes be placed?
options: Leave the whole right hemisphere unrecorded
Use needle electrodes over the defect
Place electrodes over the bone flap as usual
Move the left homologue to match; note the defect
questions.explanation: Use at least 16 electrodes, note skull defects, drains and bolts, and when an electrode must be moved, move its homologue symmetrically so the hemispheres can still be compared. Over a skull defect, a breach effect (higher-amplitude, sharper, faster activity) is expected and its location should be given.
questions.memoryAid: MOVE ONE, MOVE ITS TWIN: keep left and right comparable.
